title: Evaluation for finite locally free module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module: there is an open cover $(V_a)$ of $X$ such that $\mathcal F|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$ for integers $d_a\geq0$ (compare the constant-rank notion of [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]). For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, the canonical evaluation morphism $\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$, where $\mathcal F^{\vee}:=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, natural in $\mathcal G$. Here tensor product, sheaf Hom, its group of global sections, and sheaves of modules use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module], and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Let P be the presheaf tensor product F^vee tensor_{p,O} G and Q = Hom_O(F,G), a sheaf of O-modules by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For every open U define e_U: F^vee(U) tensor_{O(U)} G(U) -> Hom_{O|_U}(F|_U,G|_U) by phi tensor g |-> (x in F(W) |-> phi_W(x) g|_W for W subset U open); it is O(U)-bilinear and compatible with restriction, so e: P -> Q is a morphism of presheaves of O-modules. Now let U be contained in some V_a, so F|_U is identified with O_U^{+d_a} [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module, applied with the open cover of the statement]. An O|_U-linear map O_U^{+d} -> G|_U is determined by the images of the d standard basis sections in G(U), and every d-tuple occurs (sectionwise definition of morphisms in Mod(O) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]); hence F^vee(U) = O(U)^{+d_a}, Q(U) = G(U)^{+d_a}, P(U) = O(U)^{+d_a} tensor_{O(U)} G(U) = G(U)^{+d_a}, and under these identifications e_U is the identity of G(U)^{+d_a} ((g_1,...,g_{d_a}) |-> the map (x_1,...,x_{d_a}) |-> sum_i x_i g_i). So e_U is bijective for every open U contained in some V_a.

The open sets U contained in some V_a cover every open of X. Hence e is locally injective and locally surjective in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] (site of open subsets of X): if e_U(s)=e_U(t), then s and t agree on the cover (U cap V_a)_a, and every t in Q(U) has preimages on the members of that cover, by Step 1. By that lemma the sheafification e^#: P^# -> Q^# is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves; since Q is a sheaf, Q -> Q^# is an isomorphism, so the morphism e-bar: F^vee tensor_O G = P^# -> Q through which e factors (the O-linear factorization of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]) is a bijective O-linear map of sheaves, whose inverse is again O-linear: e-bar is the evaluation isomorphism of O_X-modules.

For a morphism G to G' of O_X-modules, the evaluation formula commutes with applying that morphism to each coefficient g_i. Hence the global evaluation isomorphism and its inverse commute with G to G', proving naturality in G; the O-module structure and bilinearity are those of the sheaf tensor, sheaf Hom, and module Hom definitions.

lean.statement: theorem dual_tensor_hom_iso (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : ∃ e : (∀ G : X.Modules, Scheme.Modules.tensorObj (dual F) G ≅ homObj F G), (∀ G : X.Modules, (e G).hom = dualTensorHom F G) ∧ ∀ {G H : X.Modules} (g : G ⟶ H), (e G).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (𝟙 F) g = (dual F ◁ g) ≫ (e H).hom
